name: Slerp, one angle per batch sample
plain: The classic latent slerp. Each sample is flattened to a single long vector, one angle is computed for it, and the raw (not unit) endpoints are mixed with sine weights. For near-orthogonal, equal-norm latents such as Gaussian noise the norm stays about constant, which is why it is used in place of lerp for noise. Norm is not explicitly restored when the two inputs differ in length.
math:
per sample: û=a/‖a‖, v̂=b/‖b‖, ω=acos(û·v̂)
out = [sin((1−t)ω)/sin ω]·a + [sin(tω)/sin ω]·b
near-parallel handling differs by provider (see providers).
Variance: at t=0.5, ω=90°, equal variances: weights are 0.707 each, so variance is kept. Lerp would halve it.
